newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDP UP TO YR/YR 7.3 PCT IN Q3 VS 5.2 PCT Q2.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDP UP TO YR/YR 7.3 PCT IN Q3 VS 5.2 PCT Q2.

text.p: Poland's gross domestic product increased in the third quarter of 1996 to year-on-year 7.3 percent (unadjusted) from 5.2 percent in the second quarter, deputy-head of the Central Statistical Office said on Monday.
Roman Sawinski told a news conference the increase was mainly the result of growing domestic demand on the back of fast growth of wages in real terms.
"Fast (economic) growth is the result of quick increases of consumer demand...and a rise in real wages," Sawinski said.

Sawinski said that if present sales trends continued for the rest of the year Poland should not have trouble meeting the government's annual GDP growth forecast of between five and six percent for 1996.
The Central Statistical Office (GUS) said GDP bottomed out at year-on-year 3.5 percent growth in the first quarter of this year after growing by seven percent in 1995.
